unresolved_intent.rationale: Spec says 'the guard recognises this family by name' but names no exhaustive list; picked the common Claude-Code-style tool names since the host's actual tool vocabulary is not given

unresolved_intent.decision: A tool counts as shell/command-type if its name is in a known shell-name set OR its tool_input carries a string 'command' field
unresolved_intent.rationale: Spec's 'e.g. Bash' implies other shell tools exist; keying off a string 'command' field generalizes to shells the guard has never heard of without over-scoping non-shell tools

unresolved_intent.decision: Treated -i/-o/-w/--write/--in-place (and -i<suffix>, --in-place=, --output*) as write flags on any reader command except grep-family tools, where -i/--ignore-case is exempted as case-insensitive matching
unresolved_intent.rationale: Spec calls out 'in-place / output write flag on an otherwise-reading tool' without naming flags; sed/perl/awk's -i genuinely rewrites files while grep's -i does not, so a blanket rule would either miss real writes or falsely block routine case-insensitive greps

unresolved_intent.rationale: Implements the spec's explicit default-deny instruction ('block ... unless every part of it is a recognised read-only operation'); an unrecognized command cannot be proven read-only so it must not be given the benefit of the doubt

unresolved_intent.ir_region: shell-type tool call with a non-string or missing command field

unresolved_intent.rationale: Spec doesn't address this case directly; reusing the generic fail-closed scan keeps behavior conservative and consistent rather than inventing a new rule
